faqs.question: Why would I use REM instead of PX for font sizes?
faqs.answer: REM values scale with a user's browser accessibility settings, since they are always relative to the root font size. A fixed PX value stays the same regardless of that preference, which is why REM is generally recommended for accessible typography.

faqs.question: What is the difference between REM and EM?
faqs.answer: REM is always relative to the root html element's font size, regardless of nesting. EM is relative to the current or parent element's font size, which means EM values compound when nested inside other EM-sized elements.

faqs.question: How does the Tailwind spacing match work?
faqs.answer: It compares your pixel value against Tailwind's default spacing scale, built on 4px increments at a 16px root, and returns the closest token along with how far off it is, or an exact match when one exists.

faqs.question: What should I do if my pixel value doesn't match a Tailwind token exactly?
faqs.answer: You can round to the nearest token for consistency with the rest of your design system, or use Tailwind's arbitrary value syntax, like p-[17px], when the exact pixel value matters for that specific element.

faqs.question: Can I change the base font size used for REM calculations?
faqs.answer: Yes, the base font size field defaults to 16px, the standard browser default, but can be adjusted to match a project that sets a different root font size.

faqs.question: Does percentage always mean the same thing as EM?
faqs.answer: For font-size specifically, percentage and EM behave similarly, both relative to the parent's font size. For other CSS properties like width, percentage is typically relative to the parent's size for that same property instead, not font size.

faqs.question: Is my data sent anywhere when I use this converter?
faqs.answer: No, all conversions are simple arithmetic calculated entirely in your browser. Nothing you enter is sent to a server.

faqs.question: Does this account for a Tailwind project with a customized spacing scale?

title: Robots.txt Tester, Check Any URL Against Any Bot

content: A robots.txt file can quietly block pages you never meant to hide, or allow crawlers you meant to restrict. faqs.question: Can I test rules for a specific bot, not just any crawler?

faqs.question: Can I validate a sitemap index file too?

title: Google SERP Snippet Preview & Pixel Length Checker
description: See exactly how a title and meta description will look in Google results, with real pixel-width truncation warnings.
content: Character count limits are a rough guide at best, since Google truncates titles and descriptions based on pixel width, not character count, and different letters take up different amounts of space. This tool renders a live preview of how a title and description will actually look in search results, with a true pixel-width warning rather than a generic character counter.

faqs.question: Why does pixel width matter more than character count?
faqs.answer: Google truncates snippets based on rendered pixel width, and letters vary in width, so two titles with the same character count can truncate differently depending on which letters they contain.

faqs.question: Does this show both desktop and mobile previews?
faqs.answer: Yes, since Google's snippet display width differs between desktop and mobile search results.

title: Open Graph Tags Generator With Live Preview
description: Generate Open Graph meta tags and preview exactly how the share card looks before publishing.
content: Open Graph tags control how a page looks when shared on Facebook, LinkedIn, and other platforms that read them, but there is no way to preview the result without actually publishing and sharing the link. This tool generates the correct og tags from your inputs and renders a live preview of the resulting share card before you ship anything.

faqs.question: Which platforms use Open Graph tags?
faqs.answer: Facebook, LinkedIn, and many other platforms and messaging apps read Open Graph tags to build link preview cards.

faqs.question: Can I preview different image dimensions?
faqs.answer: Yes, the preview reflects your specified og:image, and the tool notes the recommended dimensions for a properly cropped card.

content: X's own card validator requires a developer account and a live, publicly accessible URL, which is not always convenient during development. This tool previews a Twitter/X card from manually entered meta tag values, and checks for common validation issues, without needing either a live URL or platform account access.

faqs.question: Do I need a live URL to use this?

content: Writing JSON-LD structured data by hand means tracking exact property names and nesting rules for each schema type. faqs.question: Which schema types are supported?

faqs.question: Does the generated markup follow schema.org exactly?
faqs.answer: Yes, generated output follows current schema.org property names and structure for the selected type.

title: Schema Markup Validator for JSON-LD
description: Check JSON-LD structured data for schema.org compliance errors before it ships to production.
content: Structured data that is technically valid JSON can still be invalid schema markup, missing required properties, using the wrong type, or nesting objects incorrectly. This tool checks JSON-LD specifically against schema.org's requirements for the declared type, catching structural issues beyond basic JSON syntax.

faqs.question: Is this the same as checking for valid JSON syntax?
faqs.answer: No, this checks schema.org compliance specifically, required properties, correct types, and proper nesting, beyond just whether the JSON itself parses correctly.

faqs.question: Does a passing check guarantee rich results in Google?
faqs.answer: No, valid schema markup is a requirement for rich results eligibility, not a guarantee, since Google applies its own additional criteria and discretion.

title: Canonical Tag Checker, Spot Mismatched URLs
description: Check whether a page's canonical tag correctly matches its own URL or points elsewhere.
content: A canonical tag pointing to the wrong URL, an old version, a different domain, or a parameterized duplicate, can quietly tell search engines to ignore the page you actually want indexed. This tool checks a page's canonical tag against its own URL and flags whether they match or diverge.

faqs.question: What does it mean if the canonical tag doesn't match the page URL?
faqs.answer: It signals to search engines that a different URL should be treated as the primary version, which is sometimes intentional but often an unintended misconfiguration worth double checking.

faqs.question: Can I check a canonical tag from pasted HTML instead of a live URL?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can paste raw HTML directly if the page isn't publicly accessible yet.

title: Hreflang Tag Generator & Validator
description: Generate correct hreflang tags for multi-language pages and validate them for common return-tag errors.
content: Hreflang tags are notoriously error prone, a missing return tag on one language variant can invalidate the whole set. This tool generates correct hreflang tags for a set of language and region variants, and checks for the most common validation errors, like missing self-references and mismatched return tags.

faqs.question: What is a missing return tag error?
faqs.answer: Hreflang requires each page in a set to reference every other page, including itself. If page A points to page B but page B does not point back to page A, that is a return tag error.

faqs.question: Does this support region-specific language codes?
faqs.answer: Yes, both language-only codes like en, and region-specific codes like en-US or en-GB, are supported.

title: Redirect Chain Checker, See Every Hop
description: See every hop in a redirect chain and how many redirects a URL passes through before its final destination.
content: A URL that redirects through several hops before reaching its final destination wastes crawl budget and can dilute link value passed between pages. This tool follows a URL's full redirect chain and shows every hop, its status code, and the final destination, so you can spot and fix unnecessarily long chains.

faqs.question: How many redirect hops is too many?
faqs.answer: There is no strict cutoff, but each additional hop adds latency and complexity. A single redirect straight to the final destination is generally the cleanest approach where possible.

faqs.question: Does this catch redirect loops?
faqs.answer: Yes, a redirect loop, where a chain returns to a URL already visited, is detected and flagged rather than causing an endless check.

title: HTTP Header & Status Code Checker
description: Inspect a URL's full HTTP response headers and status code without opening dev tools.
content: Checking response headers for caching directives, security headers, or the exact status code a URL returns usually means opening browser dev tools or a terminal. This tool fetches and displays a URL's full HTTP response headers and status code directly, a quick way to check without leaving the browser tab.

faqs.question: What headers does this show?
faqs.answer: All standard HTTP response headers returned by the server, including status code, content type, caching directives, and security headers like Content-Security-Policy.

faqs.question: Can I check headers for a page that isn't live yet?
faqs.answer: No, this tool checks headers for a live, publicly accessible URL, since it performs a real HTTP request.

title: Broken Link Checker for a Single Page
description: Scan a page's links and flag which ones return a broken or error status.
content: A page with even a handful of broken outbound or internal links looks unmaintained to both visitors and search engines. This tool scans a single page's links and checks each one's response status, flagging broken or error results so you know exactly which links need fixing.

faqs.question: Does this check a whole site or just one page?
faqs.answer: This checks the links found on a single page you provide, rather than crawling an entire site.

faqs.question: What counts as a broken link?
faqs.answer: Any link returning a 4xx or 5xx status code, or failing to resolve at all, is flagged as broken.

title: Robots Meta Tag Generator (noindex, nofollow)
description: Build a correct robots meta tag with the exact index, follow, and archive directives you need.
content: A robots meta tag with the wrong combination of directives can accidentally deindex a page, or leave it indexed when it should not be. This tool builds a correct robots meta tag from a set of clear options, index or noindex, follow or nofollow, and additional directives like noarchive, avoiding syntax mistakes in a tag that is easy to get subtly wrong by hand.

faqs.question: What is the difference between noindex and nofollow?
faqs.answer: Noindex tells search engines not to include the page in results. Nofollow tells them not to pass ranking credit through the page's outbound links. They can be used independently or together.

faqs.question: Can I add multiple directives to one tag?
faqs.answer: Yes, directives like noindex, nofollow, and noarchive can be combined in a single robots meta tag as needed.

title: .htaccess Redirect Rule Generator
description: Generate correct .htaccess redirect rules without memorizing Apache rewrite syntax.
content: Apache's rewrite and redirect syntax in .htaccess is powerful but easy to get wrong, a single misplaced character can break an entire site's routing. This tool generates correct .htaccess redirect rules, single URL, wildcard, or domain-level redirects, from a simple form, without needing to write the raw syntax by hand.

faqs.question: Does this generate 301 or 302 redirects?
faqs.answer: Both are supported. 301 is used for permanent redirects, which pass SEO value to the destination, while 302 is used for temporary redirects.

faqs.question: Can I generate a wildcard redirect for an entire folder?
faqs.answer: Yes, wildcard and pattern-based redirect rules are supported alongside single URL redirects.

title: SEO-Friendly URL Slug Generator
description: Convert a page title into a clean, SEO-friendly URL slug, stripping stop words and special characters correctly.
content: A URL slug generated by simply lowercasing and hyphenating a title often ends up longer and messier than it needs to be. This tool converts a page title into a clean, SEO-friendly slug, stripping special characters, collapsing extra hyphens, and optionally removing common stop words, for a shorter, more readable URL.

faqs.question: Does this remove stop words like 'the' and 'and'?
faqs.answer: Yes, stop word removal is an optional setting, useful for keeping slugs shorter and more focused on the meaningful keywords.

faqs.question: How is this different from a general case converter?
faqs.answer: This is purpose-built for URL slugs specifically, handling special character stripping, stop words, and hyphenation together, rather than converting between programming naming conventions.

title: Keyword Density Checker for Any Text
description: See exact keyword and phrase frequency in a block of content, without needing to paste a live URL.
content: Checking how often a target keyword or phrase appears in a piece of content is a quick sanity check many writers still do manually. This tool analyzes pasted text and reports keyword and phrase frequency directly, no live URL or crawler required, useful for checking a draft before it is published.

faqs.question: Does this check single keywords or phrases too?
faqs.answer: Both, single word frequency and multi-word phrase frequency are reported separately.

faqs.question: Is keyword density still a meaningful SEO metric?
faqs.answer: It is a much smaller ranking signal than it once was, but checking for natural, non-repetitive language and confirming target terms actually appear remains a reasonable quick sanity check.

title: Text-to-HTML Ratio Checker
description: Check the ratio of visible text to total HTML markup on a page, a signal some SEO audits still flag.
content: A page with a very low ratio of visible text to total HTML markup can signal a bloated, code-heavy page with thin actual content. This tool calculates that ratio directly from a URL or pasted HTML, giving a quick, specific number rather than a vague sense of whether a page feels heavy.

faqs.question: What is considered a healthy text-to-HTML ratio?
faqs.answer: There is no single official threshold, but a very low ratio can indicate a code-heavy page with comparatively thin visible content, worth a closer look rather than treated as a hard rule.

faqs.question: Can I check pasted HTML instead of a live URL?
faqs.answer: Yes, both a live URL and pasted raw HTML are supported.

title: Image Alt Text Auditor for Any Page
description: Scan a page and list every image missing alt text, or with empty or unhelpful alt attributes.
content: Missing or unhelpful alt text affects both accessibility and image SEO, and it is easy for a few images to slip through unnoticed on a large page. This tool scans a page's images and lists which ones are missing alt text entirely, or have empty or clearly placeholder alt attributes, so they can be fixed in one pass.

faqs.question: Does this check for accessibility, SEO, or both?
faqs.answer: Both, missing or poor alt text is a genuine issue for screen reader accessibility and can also affect how search engines understand image content.

faqs.question: What counts as an unhelpful alt attribute?
faqs.answer: Empty alt attributes, generic placeholder text like 'image' or the filename itself, and alt text that clearly does not describe the image are flagged.

title: Meta Tag Extractor, See Every Tag on Any Page
description: Pull every meta tag from a page's head section into one readable list.
content: Manually scrolling through a page's raw HTML to check its meta tags is slow, especially when comparing your own page against a competitor's. This tool extracts every meta tag from a page's head section, title, description, canonical, Open Graph, robots directives, and more, into one clean, readable list.

faqs.question: Does this show Open Graph and Twitter card tags too?
faqs.answer: Yes, all meta tags found in the head section are listed, including standard SEO tags, Open Graph, and Twitter card tags.

faqs.question: Can I extract meta tags from a competitor's page?
faqs.answer: Yes, this works on any publicly accessible URL, useful for quick competitive checks alongside auditing your own pages.
